bandReport.notes:
Band covers items 66-80 and ends the paper at item 80. Filled itemsByPage page by page while reading; no page in the band was empty and none was skipped.

COMPLETENESS. Item 66 begins at the top of p34-c1 and is whole; item 80 ends on p42-c2 with all four options and is whole. Nothing runs into or out of the band.

TERRITORY I DO NOT OWN. I opened p32 (band b4's page) to check whether any Directions block or shared preamble started there and carried into my first page. It does not: p32 holds items 63, 64 and 65, each complete on that page, and item 65 (a data-sufficiency item) ends with its full option block in the right column. So there is no passage or directions preamble spanning the p32/p34 boundary, and my item 66 stands alone. I did not transcribe p32's items.

SHARED PASSAGES. Only one Directions block falls in this band, on p38: 'Directions for the following 2 (two) items :' followed by two passages. Passage-1 (poetry / absolute truths) governs item 71 ONLY; Passage-2 (the flower / pollen) governs item 72 ONLY. Each item's own passage is in its context; the directions preamble is NOT in context. Because each passage governs exactly one item, no passage text is repeated, so there is no cross-item byte-identity risk here. Item 71's and item 72's stems and options are distinct, so nothing collides on content_hash.

SLICED CROPS. p38-c2 and p42-c2 both carry a narrow vertical strip of the LEFT column's line-ends bleeding down their left edge (on p38-c2 the fragments 'er/ur/on', 'ot/1s./ve/rn' etc. are the tails of Passage-1's lines). The right-column content itself is complete in both, but because the split was clearly off I re-read both pages from p38.png and p42.png and confirmed the right column word for word. No content was lost or misattributed. p34, p36 and p40 crops are clean; I still cross-checked each against its full page.

FINAL-PAGE CHECK. p42 is the last page of the band and its right column is NOT sparse - it carries items 78, 79 and 80 in full. I verified against p42.png that nothing sits below item 80 on either column; the page ends with option (d) of item 80, the footer 'KSPC-B-GSPT/61A', page number 43 and '[ P.T.O.' The [ P.T.O. is the booklet's standing footer and does not imply a further English item; the paper's 80 items are complete here. p42 is also the one page in the band with no Hindi shadow-through.

PRINTED ODDITIES, all transcribed verbatim, none corrected:
- Item 78 prints the second code word with a space inside the opening quote: ‘ TRAP’, where ‘POT’ on the same line is set tight. Transcribed with the space as printed. Verified at 2.6x zoom.
- Item 76 uses the struck relational glyphs ≯ (not greater than) and ≮ (not less than) inside the quoted definitions; written as \ngtr and \nless. Verified at zoom - they are struck-through > and < , not ordinary ones.
- Item 76's statement lines are set with irregular spacing around the parenthesised operators ('2x (S)3y', '9y(P) 8z'); I collapsed that typesetting space, since it carries no meaning, and kept the operator order exactly.
- Item 79 prints an asterisk as the unknown term. I wrapped both occurrences as math (\(*\)) so a markdown renderer cannot read the pair as emphasis delimiters; the printed character is a plain asterisk.
- The paper sets the statement labels with an en dash: 'Statement–I', 'Statement–II'. Preserved as printed (U+2013), which is visibly longer than the hyphen the same page uses in 'by-product'.
- Item 69 prints the rupee sign with a space before the amount (₹ 50, ₹ 16). Preserved.

No option was reordered anywhere in this band, and no item printed its options out of numeric/alphabetic order. No duplicate option texts were found - item 78's four near-anagrams (AARENA / AANREA / AANEAR / AANERA) were checked individually at 2.6x zoom and are all distinct. Every item in the band has exactly four options.

Items 66, 67, 68, 69, 70 and 73 are the data-sufficiency family. Following the brief, each one's 'Question :' and 'Statement–I / Statement–II' lines are kept in the STEM (not context), because those lines are what distinguish otherwise-identical items and the shared four options would otherwise collapse them onto one content_hash.

questions.stem:
A Question is given followed by two Statements I and II. Consider the Question and the Statements.
Question :
If the average marks in a class are 60, then what is the number of students in the class?
Statement–I :
The highest marks in the class are 70 and the lowest marks are 50.
Statement–II :
Exclusion of highest and lowest marks from the class does not change the average.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above Question and the Statements?

options.label: A
options.text: The Question can be answered by using one of the Statements alone, but cannot be answered using the other Statement alone

options.label: B
options.text: The Question can be answered by using either Statement alone

options.label: C
options.text: The Question can be answered by using both the Statements together, but cannot be answered using either Statement alone

options.label: D
options.text: The Question cannot be answered even by using both the Statements together

questions.context: Unlike religion and science, poetry does not posit or expect any belief in absolute truths. Those forces or individuals who claim to have absolute truths in their grasp tend to turn dictatorial and tyrannical. Truth usually does not admit any contradictions or imperfections. It is unitarian. It is, therefore, not of much use for poetry. Poetry abides by the plurality of life and existence. Perhaps poetry follows reality which is plural, anachronistic, full of contradictions. Against the tyranny of truth, poetry remains a partisan of democratic reality. Against the arrogance of power, wealth and hierarchy, poetry proposes both humility and defiance.
questions.stem: Which one of the following statements best reflects the most logical and rational message conveyed by the above passage?

options.label: A
options.text: It is the poetry, not science or religion, which recognizes and accepts imperfections in humans.

options.label: B
options.text: Truth is revealed through science or religion and poetry is anathema to truth.

options.label: C
options.text: Poetry is romantic, imaginary and is about feeling whereas science and religion are about truth.

options.label: D
options.text: In a world of violence, tyranny and bigotry, poetry is a form of dynamic resistance.

questions.context: The flower was not invented to please us. It flaunted its petals and spread its perfume to attract an insect. The insect carries the pollen from flower to flower so that pollen is not carried away by wind and thus not wasted. What we call a flower’s beauty is merely a by-product and a human invention. The perfume is not there to please us, it pleases us because it is there and we have been conditioned to it.
